parts.title: To the Playground
parts.text: Jada, Theo, and Hana ran to the playground. Jada wanted to ride the **seesaw**. Theo sat on the other end. The ride was **bumpy**, and Jada began to laugh.

parts.title: Log Tricks
parts.text: Hana climbed onto a low log. She held out her arms to **balance**. The log began to **wobble**, but she did not fall. Theo gave her a big **grin**. He saw a butterfly and began to **tiptoe** so it would not fly away.

parts.title: Round and Round
parts.text: Next, the friends ran to the merry-go-round. It began to **spin**. Hana wanted to **twirl** in the grass, but she felt **dizzy** and sat down. A squirrel began to **scamper** up a tree. Theo tried to **chase** it. The squirrel made a big **leap** to a branch.

parts.title: A Fun Day
parts.text: The squirrel was gone. The friends sat down and drank cold water. It was a fun day at the park.

definitions.meaning1: To shake or rock from side to side. Example: The table will wobble if one leg is short.
definitions.meaning2: A shaky rocking move. Example: The bike had a little wobble.
definitions.studentChallenge: The tall block tower began to ___.

definitions.meaning1: To stay steady without falling. Example: I can balance on one foot.
definitions.meaning2: Staying steady. Example: She kept her balance on the log.
definitions.studentChallenge: Can you ___ a book on your head?

definitions.meaning1: Feeling like the room is spinning. Example: I felt dizzy after I turned in circles.
definitions.studentChallenge: After the fast ride, Sam felt ___.

definitions.meaning1: To turn around and around fast. Example: I spin in a circle on the grass.
definitions.meaning2: One fast turn. Example: The top gave a spin.
definitions.studentChallenge: Watch the wheel ___ round and round.

definitions.meaning1: To turn around and around in a light, pretty way. Example: She likes to twirl in her new dress.
definitions.meaning2: A pretty spin. Example: The dancer did a twirl.
definitions.studentChallenge: The dancer will ___ on her toes.

definitions.meaning1: To jump high or far. Example: The frog can leap over the log.
definitions.meaning2: A big jump. Example: He took a leap across the puddle.
definitions.studentChallenge: I will ___ over the little stream.

definitions.meaning1: To run after someone or something to catch it. Example: The puppy likes to chase the ball.
definitions.meaning2: A game of running after. Example: We played a fun chase.

definitions.meaning1: Full of bumps, not smooth. Example: The dirt road was bumpy.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ride in the wagon was ___.

definitions.meaning1: A big smile. Example: He had a grin from ear to ear.
definitions.meaning2: To smile big. Example: I grin when I see my friends.
definitions.studentChallenge: She had a big ___ on her face.

definitions.meaning1: To run quickly with small, light steps. Example: Mice scamper across the floor.
To walk on the tips of your toes, very quietly. Example: I tiptoe so I do not wake the baby.
definitions.meaning2: Standing on your toes. Example: She stood on tiptoe to see.

definitions.meaning1: A long board that goes up and down when two kids sit on the ends. Example: We rode the seesaw at the park.
definitions.meaning2: To go up and down like a seesaw. Example: The boat seemed to seesaw on the waves.
definitions.studentChallenge: Two kids sat on the ___ and went up and down.
